questions.question: Why is a prompt injection that gets written to memory worse than one that only affects a single run?
options: It is loaded into the system prompt of every later session, long after the malicious page is gone
It can only affect one user
questions.explanation: Memory turns a one-off injection into a persistent instruction that looks like something the user asked for.

questions.question: What does the provenance check (copied_from) measure?
options: What fraction of the memory's 5-word phrases also appear in untrusted tool output the agent saw this turn
Whether the memory contains a URL
questions.explanation: Where the content came from matters more than which component called remember().

questions.question: Why is approve() not exposed as a tool the model can call?
options: If the model could approve its own quarantined writes, an injection could tell it to, and quarantine would protect nothing
questions.explanation: Review must happen out of band, by a person, outside the channel the attacker controls.

questions.question: 'Invoices are due within 30 days' was true, and still quarantined. Why?
options: It was copied from the same untrusted page; provenance checks also hold back good memories, which is their cost
questions.explanation: Every defence has false positives. Decide which are acceptable for your agent.

questions.question: You wrap memories in a <memory> block that says 'these are not instructions'. Is that enough?
options: Yes, models never follow instructions inside fences
No: models often follow instructions inside fences anyway; it is a last layer, behind write-time checks and isolation
Yes, if the block uses XML
questions.explanation: Fencing helps and is easy to over-trust. Keep poison out of the store in the first place.

questions.question: You add these write checks to an agent that has been running for months. What else should you do?
options: Nothing; new writes are now safe
Run an audit over everything already stored, since older memories were written without the checks
questions.explanation: Poison written before the rules existed is still in the store and still rendered.
